output.brief: The evidence points to bad data, not operators. In early October, Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month shelf life for Veltranol with a valid-from date of March 2027. The original 24-month value stayed in place. Printer records show that from 4 Oct the line integration service sent 36 months to the printers. Every job from then on printed an expiry 12 months too late. No operator overrides were made, and the camera passed every carton because it only checks the print against the job. Before 4 Oct all 30 jobs were correct, including jobs run by the new agency operators after the firmware change. That rules out the operators and the firmware as causes. Two permanent day-shift jobs on Line 1 were also wrong, so the fault is not limited to Line 3 nights, and those two lots are in the warehouse. I'm not sure why the integration service ignored the future valid-from date. Ask the vendor and IT to explain that. I'm fairly confident the cause is the master-data edit. Do not discipline the agency staff, and keep the camera check on. Reset the Veltranol record, extend the hold to every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, and add a second-person check of each printed expiry. Inspect retained cartons of the two other products whose edits carry future dates (HX-15-30 and MR-05-14). Do not over-label stock yet.
